reason: virtualAssets == 0 is the one-time initialization sentinel for a private appended storage slot. Every reserve quote is at least one (or VIRTUAL_SHARES for an empty series), and the final-exit reset writes VIRTUAL_SHARES rather than zero. Token balances cannot clear this slot. Equality selects initialization, not a target asset balance. stQEUROToken tests cover legacy activation, preview/settlement agreement, exits to dust, loss after activation, and empty-series reset.

Both callers (creditVaultYield and harvestAndDistributeVaultYield) hold nonReentrant throughout pricing admission and settlement. The linked pricing library calls the configured module; the deployed module has no mutable external callbacks. Price-cache initialization is governance-only. MintExecutionBoundaryAudit explicitly tests adversarial module callbacks into both yield entrypoints, public minting, and initializePriceCache. The flagged internal helper cannot be entered externally.

The function directly returns all three ExecutionPricingLibrary.mint results to its caller. Slither misidentifies the direct tuple return as unused; combined-release integration verifies the resulting mint amount and backing.

The current price, oracle-computed staleness and bounds flags are checked. Historical fallback price and raw update time are deliberately unused; the active oracle computes freshness from its update time.
Timestamp comparisons intentionally enforce monotonic observations, reject future or expired depth, and prevent depth reuse before hedge acknowledgment.
Timestamp comparisons intentionally reject future, expired, regressing or pre-configuration capacity observations.
Depth and account observations deliberately expire after the configured maximum age; timestamps are used for freshness, not randomness.

The function returns the linked accounting library's three reward amounts directly to the caller through a tuple return. Slither misidentifies the direct tuple return as unused, the same pattern as QuantillonVault._computeMintAmounts. The library performs every state update itself; HedgerPoolInterestRewardAccrual and HedgerPool tests assert the returned amounts.

manage() is the single dispatcher of the Propose/Accept/Execute/Cancel ownership-transfer state machine. Each action is a linear run of authorization, exact proposal binding, freshness and recipient-state checks that must read and update one shared proposal record; splitting them across functions would duplicate the invariants without removing any. The library is a deployed linked unit, so a refactor is a versioned redeploy, not a static-analysis edit. HedgerMigration exercises every action and rejection path (authorities, pause, expiry, replaced proposals, dirty recipient, closed position, exact binding).

Proposal expiry is deliberately time-based: a proposal must expire within seven days of creation, and Accept/Execute reject it once block.timestamp passes expiresAt. The timestamp is used for freshness only; a few seconds of validator drift cannot create or extend authority because every step still requires the proposer, the recipient and paused governance. HedgerMigration tests the expired and replaced-proposal rejections.

Request deadlines (at most 15 minutes ahead), the per-action cooldown and the daily usage bucket intentionally compare block.timestamp. The comparisons rate-limit an already whitelisted operator and reject stale requests; they are not used for randomness or ordering. QuantillonRebalancerModule tests cover nonce, deadline and cooldown handling and the day-boundary usage accounting.

Derives the current day from block.timestamp to decide whether the previous day's spend still counts toward the rolling 48-hour window limit. The bucket boundary only affects how quickly the rate limit relaxes; the operator cannot exceed maxWindowUsdc by shifting a few seconds. Covered by the midnight and reconfiguration usage tests in QuantillonRebalancerModule.

positions() is the public HedgePosition getter and returns the full struct tuple. The destructuring intentionally reads only hedger and isActive to verify the Safe still owns the live position; the other components are irrelevant to the authorization check. Slither reports any partially consumed tuple as unused.

positions() and coreParams() are public struct getters returning full tuples. The floor check intentionally reads only qeuroBacked (the EUR liability) and minMarginRatio (the contract floor); the other components are not needed. Slither reports partially consumed tuples as unused.

Deliberate raw call forwarding so destination revert data propagates unchanged. Both targets are immutable, code-checked at deployment and distinct from the writer; calldata must start with the pinned updateSlippageBatch/publish selectors; no ETH or delegatecall is involved; and only the immutable writer may call, so a destination cannot reenter. The contract is deployed non-upgradeable. PublicationBatcher tests cover exact forwarding, revert propagation and rollback, reentrancy and selector restrictions.

The withdrawal entrypoint is nonReentrant and settles the external-vault principal before updating totalUsdcHeld. The only callback-capable adapter is reached through the configured staking adapter set, whose withdrawals are governed by the same guard and validated accounting path; reentry cannot observe or mutate an intermediate settlement state.

HedgerPoolAccountingLibrary.checkpoint returns the pending amount for callers that need to expose it, while this internal checkpoint helper deliberately uses the library for its storage updates only. The reward state and accrual clock are the consumed effects, and reward accounting tests cover each exposure mutation checkpoint.

Redemption capacity and oracle observations intentionally expire after the configured maximum age. These timestamp comparisons enforce freshness and reject future observations; they are not used for randomness or authorization.
The degraded haircut is available only while the capacity observation remains fresh. The timestamp comparison intentionally bounds the fallback window and does not influence randomness or authority.

This internal redemption path is entered only through the nonReentrant redemption entrypoint. External principal withdrawal completes before the price cache and collateral totals are committed, and the adapter set is governance-controlled; the flagged ordering cannot be reentered through an externally callable path.

Liquidation redemption is reached through the guarded liquidation flow. Principal withdrawal uses the configured adapter set and all post-call writes are settlement bookkeeping under the same nonReentrant boundary; no external caller can enter this internal helper between those writes.

The helper is internal and called only from nonReentrant mint, redemption and withdrawal flows. It withdraws through governance-configured adapters and then updates the aggregate principal counter; the reported cross-function path is unreachable during an external callback.

setSingleHedger delegates to HedgerPoolAccountingLibrary.assignSingleHedger, which performs the governance authorization and explicit zero-address rejection before returning the assigned address. Slither cannot follow this linked-library validation from the wrapper and reports the assignment location without a function name.

This legacy reward calculator rounds down before a bonus calculation. UserPool has no reward claim/mint path and exposes zero live rewards; the unused calculation cannot transfer assets or affect the active ERC4626 staking flow.
The zero-amount guard intentionally handles an empty payout or vesting balance. Positive values follow the payout/vesting path; it is not an equality against a manipulable nonzero balance.

Zero-yield return avoids a no-op withdrawal; exact USDC balance deltas reject nonstandard transfers and zero burned shares. These checks validate settlement amounts, not a manipulable external target balance.
Exact day-bucket selection deliberately distinguishes the current and immediately previous bucket; the rolling sum retains both. Day-boundary limit tests exercise the transitions.

The unvestedBalance == 0 check returns zero when no yield remains to vest. It intentionally tests an empty internal accounting balance, not equality to a manipulable nonzero external balance. Vesting preview and settlement tests cover empty, partially vested and fully vested balances.
Exact day-bucket selection deliberately distinguishes the current and immediately previous bucket; the rolling sum retains both. Day-boundary limit tests exercise the transitions.

A zero-share deposit must revert. The neighboring redeem-value check bounds ERC4626 rounding loss; donation and inflation regression tests verify rejection.

The linked transfer helper is delegatecalled only by QuantillonVault._mintQEUROCommit. That commit entrypoint is onlySelf, and its nonReentrant public parent binds payer to msg.sender before the explicit self-call. Moving the transfer into a linked library did not make payer externally selectable; signed protocol settlement tests exercise the complete guarded path.

The two reported transfers share one onlySelf commit helper. Its nonReentrant public caller binds hedger to msg.sender before the explicit self-call, so an external caller cannot select another allowance owner. HedgerPool position tests cover both the net-margin transfer and the separately routed entry fee.

Migration verifies the resulting principal, underlying assets, USDC deltas, registry binding and tracked principal directly. The deposit return and fourth registry tuple field add no authority or accounting information; rollback and exact-balance tests cover settlement.

Yield credits pass a literal zero feeRate to ExecutionPricingLibrary.mint, so its first return (Math.mulDiv(input, feeRate, 1e18)) is always zero. Net backing and QEURO output are both consumed, and the execution spread is paid separately. Yield fee and execution-spread tests cover this path.

The helper needs the configured adapter, active flag and already-tracked principal for validation and its event. Current underlying is a monitoring value and is intentionally irrelevant to a new deposit; depositUnderlying's returned shares are checked for zero. External-vault mint settlement tests cover accounting and rollback.

SignedReferenceSource.submit authenticates the report, validates freshness and independent-price bounds, and reverts on any invalid report. Its returned digest is only an informational copy of the already verified report hash; the atomic margin operation needs the resulting cached reference state, not a second copy of that digest. TypedReferenceWithdrawal tests cover valid delivery, invalid signatures and rollback.

The delegatecall deliberately preserves the original pool user and storage. The library accepts only deposit or withdraw selectors, binds the complete calldata to a signed quote before dispatch, and those two pool entrypoints retain nonReentrant. UserPool's signedRouteActive guard remains set across prepare, dispatch and finish, so recursive quote execution fails atomically.

The staticcall is a read-only feature probe for supportsSignedExecution on a proposed module after its vault binding is verified. Failure, fallback execution or malformed return data all produce false; no authority or state is transferred. Execution-pricing configuration tests cover legacy and signed modules.

The delegatecall is restricted to four explicitly enumerated HedgerPool selectors and preserves the original hedger identity. A signed reference is validated first, and each dispatched pool operation retains its existing authorization and reentrancy checks. Revert data is propagated and the reference update rolls back with a failed operation.

The private dispatcher is reached only after SignedExecutionPricing binds the caller and complete calldata to an authorized quote, or after the library constructs the fixed emergency-redeem selector itself. Delegatecall preserves the vault storage and original user, while the target vault entrypoints keep nonReentrant; failures bubble and roll back the quote context.

The timestamp arithmetic determines weekday and time-of-day solely to choose between two governance-bounded reference-divergence tolerances. It is not randomness, does not select a winner or transfer value, and a small timestamp shift can only switch between the configured normal and off-hours validation bounds. SignedReferenceSource tests cover both windows.

The public redemption entrypoint holds nonReentrant across the oracle read, signed liquidation consumption, adapter withdrawals, fee routing, burn and payout. Every reported state write is inside that guard, and the configured module and adapter callbacks cannot reenter any guarded settlement path. Signed liquidation and external-collateral redemption tests exercise these interactions.

signedRouteActive is set before the external vault preparation and remains set through the delegatecalled deposit or withdraw and finalization; recursive quote execution therefore reverts. The only permitted dispatched selectors are the pool's own nonReentrant deposit and withdraw entrypoints, and any downstream failure rolls the guard back with the transaction. Signed staking settlement tests cover both routes.

prepare is callable only by the immutable vault. Its immutable reference source validates the independent price through view/static calls; neither the reference source nor the independent source can satisfy onlyVault, and a state-changing callback under static context reverts. Nonce and active-context writes occur before vault settlement and the whole operation is atomic. SignedExecutionPricing tests cover replay and active-context rejection.

The same immutable-source and onlyVault boundaries make the reported post-submit bookkeeping unreachable from a callback. Capacity updates, nonce consumption and active quote initialization are atomic; a failed callback or validation reverts all earlier reference work. SignedExecutionPricing tests exercise stale reports, nonce replay and overlapping contexts.

Weekday and time-of-day intentionally select the normal or off-hours independent-reference divergence limit. Timestamp is used for market-hours policy, not randomness or authorization, and both limits remain capped by constructor validation.
The comparison deliberately returns an empty snapshot for a future, missing or expired signed/independent observation. It enforces freshness and cannot grant authority or improve an execution price.

The quote's observedAt, validAfter and validUntil checks intentionally enforce a maximum 45-second signed execution window and reject future, inverted or expired authorizations. Timestamp is used only for freshness; calldata, user, nonce and signatures provide authorization.
The independent reference must have a nonzero, nonfuture observation no older than maxReferenceAge. This is an explicit freshness gate and is not used for randomness or access control.

Signed reference reports deliberately reject zero, future and older-than-maxAge observations. The original timestamp is signed and replay never refreshes it; sequence and signature checks independently bind authorization.

Capacity observations intentionally expire after maxAge before new mint, redeem or yield exposure may be admitted. The timestamp can only make admission fail; signed capacity, acknowledgements and the hard maxOutstanding bound determine the limit.

Capacity reports deliberately reject zero, future and expired observations. Their signed original timestamp cannot be refreshed by replay, while monotonic sequence, acknowledgement and canonical-block checks independently prevent rollback.

The private assembly trampoline intentionally terminates the outer wrapper with the exact returndata from the statically linked SignedSettlementLibrary delegatecall. This is return-data forwarding, not an accidental early return; the library validates quote mode, binding and selector before dispatch. Signed protocol settlement tests decode and assert the forwarded results.

lastValidEurUsdPrice == 0 is the explicit uninitialized-cache sentinel. Valid EUR/USD prices are bounded far above zero, and minting stays disabled until governance or a validated oracle flow bootstraps the cache. Mint eligibility and price-cache initialization tests cover the sentinel.

Exact weekday comparisons classify UTC market-hours buckets; they do not compare a manipulable asset balance or decide authorization. Both normal and off-hours divergence limits are governance-bounded and the report remains signature- and freshness-checked.

totalUsdcInExternalVaults == 0 is an empty-collateral sentinel used only after liquid USDC is insufficient. It fails closed with InsufficientBalance; positive deficits are separately bounded by the tracked external principal. External-collateral redemption tests cover empty, partial and insufficient balances.

The Safe-only, nonReentrant migration marks completed before external calls. heldBefore and received deliberately preserve pre-operation balances for exact transfer-delta and final conservation checks; rereading them would erase those checks. Both adapters are constructor-bound and use the same USDC and underlying vault. Migration tests cover principal/yield preservation and atomic rollback on liquidity or registry failure.

addMargin, removeMargin, configure and setPaused share nonReentrant. The authorized operator executes fixed approval and pool calls through the bound Safe. beforeBalance deliberately remains the pre-operation balance so the final check enforces an exact USDC debit and any unexpected transfer reverts atomically. Rebalancer tests cover Safe fund conservation, allowance cleanup and reserve protection.

addMargin, removeMargin, configure and setPaused share nonReentrant, including across Safe execution and the oracle read. beforeBalance is intentionally the pre-withdrawal balance: the final comparison requires the Safe to receive exactly amount. Rebalancer tests cover the exact credit and rollback when position or vault solvency floors fail.

The manager-only withdrawal holds nonReentrant and reduces tracked principal before the bound ERC4626 withdrawal. balanceBefore intentionally snapshots USDC before that call; the post-call delta must equal fromVault and sharesBurned must be nonzero before funds are sent to the manager. Adapter tests verify exact withdrawals, principal accounting and the one-unit idle buffer.

The manager-only harvest shares nonReentrant with deposits, withdrawals and principal write-downs. Yield and idle balances are intentional pre-withdrawal snapshots; balanceBefore enforces the exact USDC receipt and sharesBurned is the fresh ERC4626 return, checked for zero. Adapter tests cover realized yield, liquidity caps, zero yield and preservation of principal.

This linked-library helper is reached through QuantillonVault._withdrawUsdcFromExternalVaults under the nonReentrant redemption or hedger-withdrawal entrypoints; external redemption commit helpers are onlySelf. The pre-call USDC snapshot deliberately measures each adapter receipt, which must equal both requested and returned amounts before principal is reduced. Each loop iteration takes a new snapshot. External-collateral redemption tests cover the withdrawal accounting.
